_doc: NPCs answer back. counters.<kind>_<ok|fail>: shown after every interaction verb of that kind (data/reactions.json verb_kind); approach.<kind>: when an NPC walks up to you (thanks, pity, partner, fan, confront, smitten). Each template: ask (alternatives, copy grammar ok), choices [{text, reply, effects, chance?, chance_mods?, fail_reply?, fail_effects?, cost?, verb?}], optional leave/leave_effects. Extra effects: react, grudge now|clear, owes, unrob, unspook.

ask: "Why are you helping me? Nobody helps anybody on {planet}."
"What's the catch? There's always a catch."
"I... don't know what to say. Why me?"
"Is this a Lumen prank? Where's the camera?"

reply: "Because you can." They say it like a prayer. #after_charity_ok#
They laugh, then stop laughing. "Nobody's ever said that to me."
"Of course you do." But they tell you what they know anyway.
"Knew it." They sigh, and talk.
They look at the next person in the queue. Then they buy them a noodle. It's spreading.
"Pay it forward... yeah. Yeah, I can do that."

ask: "Let me give you something back. I haven't got much, but..."
"Wait! Take this. I insist. It's all I've got."

reply: They press a ration into your hand. It's warm. It's the good kind.
A crumpled ration bar and a grin. "Don't tell my landlord."
Their eyes go wet. "I won't forget you. I mean it."
"You're impossible." They're smiling.
They lean in close.
"A secret? Okay. But you didn't hear it from me."

ask: "My #kin# is going to eat tonight because of you."
"You don't know what this means. My #kin# has been sick for weeks."

reply: A tiny flat, six people, one window. They feed you first. You don't argue.
"Honestly? {need}." They say it like a confession.
"I'm going to mention it to EVERYONE."

ask: "I don't need your pity."
"Keep it. I've got my pride, even if I haven't got lungs."
"Charity from someone like YOU? No thanks."

reply: "...Fine. Thank you. Don't make it weird."
fail_reply: "I said no." They mean it.

reply: They nod. Something in their face softens. "You're alright."
"I will."

ask: "Is this a Halcyon trick? Charity now, interest later?"
"Nothing's free. What's the contract?"

reply: They check your hands, your sleeves, your eyes. "...Huh. Okay. Thank you."
fail_reply: "That's exactly what a contract would say."

reply: "I KNEW it."

choices.text: Leave it on the kerb and walk away
reply: You don't look back. When you do, it's gone - and so is their frown.

ask: "Okay! Okay! Take my credits, just leave me alone!"
"Please - I've got #kin.a#. Here, take this."
"Whatever you want. Just - please."

reply: They empty their pockets. Not much. Everything they have.
A handful of crumpled credits, trembling.
They stare. Then nod, very slowly. "...Thank you."
"You're... letting me go?" They don't wait to find out.
You make sure the whole street hears it. Nobody on this block will cross you now.
Loud. Public. Effective. People look at the ground when you pass.

ask: "What do you WANT from me?"
"I'll do anything. What do you need?"

reply: They talk fast. Very fast.
Everything they know comes tumbling out.
"I never saw you. I don't even know what you look like."
"I will. I'll see it in my sleep."

ask: "Wait! I can be useful. I know things. I know PEOPLE."
"Don't! I can help you! Anything you need on {planet}!"

reply: "Eyes and ears. Yours. Whatever you say."
Names, places, prices. They don't stop for breath.
They scramble away and don't look back.

ask: "You think you scare me? I've been threatened by #faction#. Try harder."
"Go on then. Do something."
"Ha! Is that your scary voice?"

reply: You step back. They smirk. The street saw.
"Thought so." Somebody whistles.
One hit. They go down. Nobody's laughing now.
fail_reply: They duck. You don't. Your jaw files a complaint.

reply: You laugh. They laugh. Somehow you're friends now?
"Okay, okay - you're funny." The tension pops like a paste bubble.
fail_reply: They don't laugh. Not even a little.

ask: "Hey! HEY! Everyone, this one's threatening me!"
"You hear that, people? We've got a tough guy!"

reply: You don't flinch. The crowd decides you're not worth it. They go quiet.
fail_reply: The crowd laughs. At you. Loudly.

reply: "Okay, okay, misunderstanding." The crowd groans, disappointed.

choices.text: Pay the crowd to scatter ({cost} cr)
reply: Credits in the air. The crowd scatters. So does your reputation for being cheap.

ask: "...Why are you standing so close?"
"Is something wrong? You're smiling funny."
"Did you need something?"

reply: "Oh! Thanks. It's rented." They have no idea.

choices.text: Slip it back into their pocket
reply: Back where it belongs. They'll never know how close it was.
A quick hand, a pat on the shoulder. Returned.
You whistle the #brand# jingle. Nobody suspects the jingle.

ask: "Hey, you look lost. Need directions?"
"You new around here? Watch your pockets - thieves everywhere."

reply: They walk you halfway down the block, chatting. Your pocket feels heavy with their credits.

choices.text: Give it all back and confess
reply: "You WHAT?" A long pause. "...Nobody's ever given it back."
"Browsing the street?" They shrug.

ask: "THIEF! Give it back!"
"Hands where I can see them!"
"Oh, you've got some nerve."

reply: They snatch it back. "Don't let me see you again." But they don't call anyone.
"...Fine. Just go."

choices.text: Pay them to forget it ({cost} cr)
reply: The credits vanish into their coat. "I saw nothing. You were never here."
You run. They shout. Every head on the street turns.
You bolt. Behind you: "STOP THAT THIEF!"

ask: "I should call Paragon. Give me one reason not to."
"One good reason. Go."

reply: A long look. "...Here. Now get out of here." They give you a ration.
fail_reply: "So is everyone." They start dialling.

reply: They go very pale. No call.
fail_reply: "Then Paragon will know where YOU live."

reply: "Double? ...Fine. We never met."

ask: "Okay! You win! What do you want?"
"Enough! ENOUGH! I yield!"

reply: You offer a hand. They take it. "...Good fight." Weirdly, it was.
"No hard feelings?" None. Mostly.
They hand them over, wincing.
You don't look back. The street watches you go.

ask: "Who's NEXT?" someone in the crowd shouts. A circle has formed.
A crowd has gathered. Someone's taking bets on the rematch.

reply: The crowd roars. Somebody films it. You're a story now.

choices.text: Buy the loser a drink ({cost} cr)
reply: Two drinks, one bruise each. "Same time next week?" Weirdly - yes.
You melt into the crowd. Smart.

ask: "Had enough? Pay up and we're square."
"Stay down. Or go again. Your call."

reply: "Pleasure." They pocket it and help you up.
Second round's yours. They tap out.
fail_reply: Second round's theirs too. The pavement is very familiar now.

reply: Every step hurts. Every step is watched.

ask: "Not bad. You want to learn to fight properly?"
"You've got heart. No technique. Heart, though."

reply: Twenty painful minutes. You learn more than you lose.
"There's always a next time on {planet}."
The crowd jeers as you go.

ask: "Do that again! Can I film it?"
"You should be on #media_product#!"
"Who ARE you? Seriously?"
"My cousin needs to see this."

reply: You sign their sleeve. They'll never wash it.
Your autograph on their ration card. Priceless. Literally - it's void now.
"I'm in. Whatever it is, I'm in."
fail_reply: "Whoa, slow down. I just wanted a selfie."

choices.text: Ask them to spread the word
reply: "Leave it to me. By tonight, the whole block."

ask: "Can you do my kid's birthday? Please?"
"Would you do that at my bar? I'll pay! Sort of!"

reply: "FREE? On {planet}?" They hug you. Hard.
They pay. Gladly.
fail_reply: "Oh. Never mind."

reply: "Your loss. There's cake. Paste cake."

ask: "Was that supposed to be impressive?"
"Boo! BOOOO."
"Don't quit your day job. Do you have a day job?"

reply: Your comeback lands. They laugh despite themselves. "Okay. OKAY. That was good."
fail_reply: Your comeback does not land. It doesn't even take off.

reply: You bow. A drone applauds. One drone. It counts.
You storm off. It's the most dramatic thing they've seen all week.

ask: Someone throws a paste cup. It's a tough block.
A single slow clap. It's sarcastic.

reply: You catch it one-handed and eat it. The crowd erupts. You're a legend.
fail_reply: It hits you in the face. The crowd erupts. Not in a good way.

reply: It escalates. Of course it escalates.
You laugh first. It takes the sting out. A few people laugh WITH you.

ask: "What happened to you? You look like you used to be someone."
"Do you have somewhere to sleep tonight?"
"How did you end up like this?"

reply: They listen to all of it. Then they hug you. Nobody hugs on {planet}.
Tears, a sick nan, a repossessed dog. They give you more.
fail_reply: "That's the plot of #media_product#." They take their credits back.

reply: "Look after yourself." They mean it.

ask: "There's a shelter on the corner. I can walk you there."
"Do you need a place to stay? My couch is... technically a couch."

reply: Warm soup, a dry floor, a long sleep. You wake up stronger.
"Work? I know a guy." An hour of hauling, real credits.
fail_reply: "Nobody's hiring. Nobody's ever hiring."

reply: "Come find me if you don't."

ask: "Get a job."
"Everyone's begging. Why should I help YOU?"
"I'm two payments from begging myself."

reply: They hand you a broom. Twenty minutes later: credits, and a grudging nod.
fail_reply: "I can't even pay myself."

reply: It works. They hate that it works.
fail_reply: "Nice try." They walk off.

reply: You walk away. Head high. Stomach empty.

ask: "Begging's illegal after #time# on {planet}, you know."
"Do you have a begging licence? They check now."

choices.text: "So is breathing without a payment plan."
reply: They snort. Then they laugh. Then they give you something.
fail_reply: They don't laugh.

reply: "The ad-bridge. Paragon doesn't patrol under the ads."
You leave. The billboard behind you sells begging licences.

ask: "Pleasure doing business. I might have more work for you."
"You've got a head for this. Want in on something bigger?"
"Same time next week?"

reply: "I'll find you." They will.

choices.text: Ask for a better rate next time
reply: "For you? Fine. Ten percent."
fail_reply: "Don't push it."

reply: "Your loss."

ask: "Tell no one. #faction# takes a cut of everything on {planet}."
"Keep this quiet. The walls have ads."

reply: "I like you. We'll do more of this."
"...How much?" They pay you to keep quiet about paying you.
fail_reply: "Tell them. I'll tell them about YOU."

reply: "Good."

ask: "No deal. Unless..."
"You can't afford me. But I could afford you."
"Come back with better numbers."

reply: "Now we're talking."
They go pale. "Okay, okay. Special price."
fail_reply: "Go ahead. I'll call them first."

reply: "Your loss."

ask: "I don't deal with people from your... bracket."
"Credit check failed. Sorry. Not sorry."

reply: Their eyes go wide. "Oh! OH. Let's start again."
fail_reply: "Is that all?"

reply: "Is it though?"

choices.text: Ask who WILL deal with you
reply: "Try the noodle stall. They'll deal with anyone."

ask: "What ARE you?"
"Do that again. No - don't. Actually, do."
"I have so many questions."

reply: You tell them. All of it. Their eyes get very wide.
You smile and say nothing. It drives them wild.
"Forget WHAT?" Good.

ask: "Are you... from the future? You can tell me."
"Is this a Lumen experiment? Am I in one?"

reply: "I KNEW it." They'll tell this story forever.
"The past! What was it like? Was air free?"
"The ship? THE ship? Oh, that explains everything."

ask: "Get away from me, freak."
"I'm calling someone. I don't know who. SOMEONE."
"What is WRONG with you?"

reply: "...Okay. Okay. Sorry. It's been a long shift."
fail_reply: They back away faster.

reply: You go full weird. They run. Somebody films it.
You leave. They watch you all the way down the street.

ask: "That's it, I'm telling my nan about you."
"Are you on something? Can I have some?"

reply: "...She'd actually like you. That's the worst part."
"No, no - I'm sorry. It's the smog. Makes everyone jumpy."
fail_reply: "Too late. You're weird forever now."

reply: Nobody on {planet} will forget it. Nobody will be able to explain it either.

ask: "You know, you're alright. Can I tell you something?"
"Got a minute? I don't get to talk to many people."
"You're easy to talk to. That's rare here."

reply: They tell you. It's a lot. It matters.
They talk, and talk, and you just let them.
"#npc_life#"
"#npc_life#" They smile. "Thanks for asking."
"#pc_planet#"
"#pc_saga#"

ask: "Want to know a secret about this street?"
"Can I ask you something? Why did you come to {planet}?"

reply: They lower their voice.
You tell them about the Odd Duck, the debt, the stars. They listen like it's a show.
"#npc_life#"

ask: "I don't really want to talk."
"Not now."
"Do I know you?"

reply: They nod. A little warmer than before.
"...Fine. You're persistent. I'll give you that."
fail_reply: "I SAID not now."

reply: A snort. A giggle. A real laugh. "Okay, okay."
fail_reply: Nothing. Not even a smile.

ask: They're staring at a billboard instead of you.
They've got earbuds in. Ad-sponsored earbuds.

reply: Eventually they notice you. "Oh! Sorry. The ads hypnotise you after a while."

choices.text: Wave a hand in front of their face
reply: "Whoa - hi! Sorry!"
fail_reply: "Do you MIND?"

reply: The billboard offers you a loan. A passer-by films it. You're briefly famous.

ask: They stare at the papers. "You can't do this. I've lived on this street my whole life."
"Evicted? From the STREET? You can be evicted from a street?"
Their hands shake. "Where am I supposed to go?"

reply: They gather what little they own and walk. Nobody on the block looks at you the same way.
"...You'd do that?" They tear up the papers with you. They stay - and they won't forget it.
"And tell your friends." They do. Everyone on {planet} hears what your family's lawyers can do.

ask: "Hey! {name}! I've been looking for you. I owe you - what do you want?"
"There you are! I told everyone about you. And I've got something for you."

reply: They hand you a medkit wrapped in a #brand# flyer. "Stay alive, okay?"
They pull you into a doorway and whisper.
"Then I'll help the next one. And they'll help the next." A follower is born.

ask: "I couldn't let you leave without paying you back. Close your eyes. Okay, open."

reply: Credits. A whole roll of them, saved up a coin at a time.
They can't speak. They just nod.
"I already have. Everyone."

ask: "I've been worried about you. Have you eaten?"
"You looked rough earlier. I brought you something."

reply: Hot paste and something green. You feel almost human.
You split it. You both laugh with your mouths full.
"You're not. But okay."

ask: "You're bleeding again. Sit. Let me look at that."
"I asked around. The clinic owes me a favour. Want it?"

reply: Clumsy hands, kind eyes. It helps more than you expected.
"Tell them I sent you." A free check-up. Painkillers too.

choices.text: "Save it for someone who needs it."
reply: "YOU need it." But they respect it.

ask: "Psst. {name}. Air canisters that fell off a truck. Two for twenty?"
"Got some canisters. Mountain Fresh. Mostly. Twenty for two?"

reply: "Pleasure. Don't sniff them in public."
"Fine. Ten. You're killing me."
fail_reply: "Twenty or nothing."

reply: "Your lungs."

ask: "Hold this package for me. Don't open it. I'll pay you now."
"Quick job: carry this across the block. Thirty-five credits."

reply: Easy money. Probably legal. Definitely money.
fail_reply: Paragon scanners ping. The package was not what they said.
A drone flags the package. You drop it and run - but it got your face.

reply: Inside: #found_item#. You hand it back. They're annoyed, but they respect it.
"Suit yourself. More for me."

ask: "I know where a #faction# courier drops off. Fifty-fifty?"
"Got a tip worth real credits. Fifteen to hear it."

reply: The tip is good. Very good.
fail_reply: The tip was stale. The drop moved yesterday.

reply: You make a call. Paragon thanks you. Your partner will never speak to you again.
"Your loss, partner."

ask: "OH MY GOD it's {name}! Can I get a selfie? Please?"
"I've told EVERYONE about you. Will you sign my air canister?"
"Are you THE {name}?"

reply: Flash. It's already online. #small_num# likes and climbing.
They clutch it to their chest like a newborn.

choices.text: Ask them to join your cause
reply: "Yes. YES. What do I do?"
fail_reply: "Oh - I just wanted the selfie."

ask: "I started a fan club! It's just me. And my cousin. Will you come to the first meeting?"

reply: Three people, one cake, a banner with your face spelled wrong. You've never been prouder.
They frame it. In a real frame.
"Too late. We have badges."

ask: "You! Thirty credits for what you did, or I'm calling Paragon."
"I know what you did. Pay up, or I make the call. Right now."
"Don't walk away from me. We need to settle this."

reply: They count it twice. "We're done. For now."
"...Okay. Okay. I believe you. Don't make me regret it."
fail_reply: "Sorry doesn't pay for anything." They pull out their wristpad.

reply: They go white and back away. No call.
fail_reply: "You just made it worse." They're dialling.

ask: "Remember me? I remember YOU. We're settling this, here and now."
"You thought I'd forget? On {planet}, we never forget."

reply: "Fair." They pocket it. The anger goes with it.
You hear them out. You agree to help. Somehow, that's enough.
fail_reply: "Words. Always words." The wristpad comes out.

reply: "Laugh all you like. Paragon's laughing too - on line two."

ask: "Hi... I, um, made you this."
"So... are you seeing anyone? Asking for a friend. The friend is me."

reply: A tiny hand-painted charm. It's terrible. You love it.

choices.text: Take them out for noodles ({cost} cr)
reply: Two bowls, one rainy window, a whole evening. Your wounds hurt less.
"Oh. Okay. No, that's - okay." They'll be fine. Eventually.

ask: "I wrote you a poem. It's bad. Do you want to hear it?"

reply: It rhymes 'breath' with 'debt'. It's terrible. It's the nicest thing anyone's said to you in years.
You write two lines on a noodle napkin. They keep it forever.
fail_reply: Your poem is worse than theirs. You both laugh until it hurts.

reply: "Later. Okay. I'll... be here. Later."
